task.name: A review loop cannot distinguish a change that is converging from one discovering a new sibling path each cycle, so topology is inventoried at development cost until the ceiling
task.story_text:
## Why

A review loop treats every cycle the same way: findings are raised, the developer addresses them, the
next cycle runs. That is the right shape when a change is converging — each cycle's findings are the
residue of the last, and the count falls toward zero.

It is the wrong shape when each cycle resolves the previous finding correctly and then discovers a
new instance of the same underlying problem somewhere else. Nothing is converging; the loop is
inventorying a surface nobody enumerated, one development pass at a time. The developer is not
failing — it is fixing exactly what it was shown. The reviewers are not failing — each finding is
real. But the work is discovery priced as implementation, and the loop cannot tell the difference.

Counts alone do not separate the two. A sequence of single findings can be a change closing in on
done, or a topology being walked. What distinguishes them is whether each cycle's finding is the same
concern in a new location: prior findings resolved, new siblings appearing under one invariant.

Forge already holds what is needed to tell them apart — finding text and location, whether the
previous cycle's findings were resolved, story-compliance mismatches, and the advisory's own
classification of the churn pattern. It simply never asks the question, so the loop runs to its cycle
ceiling and escalates only when the budget or cycle count is exhausted.

The cost is not marginal. In one story the pattern was visible by the third cycle and ran to the
fifth, spending about $40 across five development passes and reaching escalation with a finding still
open. An escalation at cycle three would have reached the same decision — that the framing was wrong
— for roughly half the money and forty fewer minutes.

## Example

The signature, from a real run. Each cycle resolved the prior finding and named a different path
under one invariant:

```
cycle 1   REQUEST_CHANGES  3 P1     unpriced dispatch: seated primaries
cycle 2   REQUEST_CHANGES  1 P1     unpriced dispatch: fallback_models        ← prior resolved
cycle 3   REQUEST_CHANGES  1 P1     unpriced dispatch: transport_fallback     ← prior resolved
cycle 4   REQUEST_CHANGES  1 P1     unpriced dispatch: adaptive pool primary  ← prior resolved
cycle 5   REQUEST_CHANGES  1 P1     unpriced dispatch: CLI→API same-model id  ← prior resolved
```

Contrast with genuine convergence, which the detector must not disturb:

```
cycle 1   REQUEST_CHANGES  3 P1
cycle 2   REQUEST_CHANGES  1 P1   ← a residual of cycle 1's findings, same location
cycle 3   APPROVE          0 P1
```

Wanted: at cycle 3 of the first sequence, the loop stops and routes to the escalate gate with the
pattern named, so the advisory reasons about framing rather than the developer attempting a fourth
location.

## Acceptance criteria

- A review loop detects when successive cycles resolve their predecessor's findings and raise new
  findings that are instances of the same underlying concern, and treats that as a signal distinct
  from a change that is converging.
- Detection rests on what the findings say and where they are, not on their count alone, so a falling
  count that reflects genuine convergence is unaffected and a flat count that reflects discovery is
  caught.
- On detection the story stops consuming development cycles and routes to the operator decision path,
  with the detected pattern and the sequence that produced it stated as evidence, so the decision is
  made about framing rather than about the latest finding.
- The point of detection is reached before the cycle ceiling, so the signal has value; a detector that
  can only fire on the last cycle reports what already happened.
- Where the loop is uncertain whether it is converging or discovering, it continues rather than
  stopping, so the failure mode is spending one more cycle rather than halting work that was about to
  finish.
- A story stopped this way preserves its work and its findings, and re-entry after an operator
  decision does not repeat the cycles already run.

## Out of scope

Changing the cycle ceiling, the allocation, or what a developer is permitted to attempt. This is
about recognising a pattern earlier, not about spending less per cycle.

handoff.summary: Added a deterministic, stdlib-only topology-walk detector (src/theforge/review_topology.py) that reads the coordinator's existing per-cycle finding snapshots, the classify_families trajectory store, and the finding-registry dispositions, and fires only when one non-file anchor spans three consecutive cycles whose predecessor locations were resolved and whose current findings sit at new locations. Wired it into review_phase.py: the signal is computed after family classification (so it reaches the trajectory sidecar and audit record on every cycle) and routed to the existing escalate gate before the max-review-cycles branch, guarded on review_cycle staying below the ceiling and on not having routed before. The triggering cycle is appended to cycle_history once, with a new history_already_appended flag on _run_escalate_gate so the gate's approve paths do not append it a second time and evict an earlier cycle from the three-entry window. A gate continue clears the escalation and re-enters the normal RETRY_DEV flow without decrementing review_cycle, so cycles already run are not replayed. The signal persists through save/load_trajectory_state, is emitted as a top-level audit key (schema bumped 26 to 27 with _migrate_v26_to_v27 and a new v27 fixture), is added to PRIOR_GENERATION_WORK_KEYS, and is carried into EvidencePacket plus a dedicated section of the advisor prompt, whose introduction no longer claims the review cycles were exhausted when they were not.

(1) The detector's requirement that family members' descriptions differ across the window rejected valid walks: reviewers routinely describe one invariant in identical words at each place it is violated, so the clearest-stated walks were the ones suppressed. Where the flag is False the pattern still renders — as supporting evidence about the churn rather than as the cause. Note this is deliberately distinct from review_topology_escalated, which is a run-lifetime latch preventing re-escalation and would have produced the same false framing if reused. No audit-schema change this iteration; the trigger is already unambiguous in the recorded escalation reason and reaches the operator via the pending decision file's evidence_packet.

story_deviations: The plan's Step 3 said to leave the interactive surface to a separate branch. Interactive and non-interactive both route through _run_escalate_gate, because that function already dispatches on the available surface (pending-file / remote / tty / none).

The plan named tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v23.json; the repository is at v26, so CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION was bumped to 27 with MIGRATION_HELPERS[26] = _migrate_v26_to_v27 and a generated tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v27.json.

Added a docs/guides/inputs-reference.md note under retry.max_review_cycles, since the ceiling's meaning changed and an operator reading the config would otherwise not learn a story can escalate earlier.

review_topology_triggered is deliberately NOT emitted as its own audit key. Doing so would require a v27-to-v28 bump for information the record already carries unambiguously: the escalation reason string names the trigger ('Topology walk detected at review cycle 3 of 5' vs 'Max cycles (N) exhausted'), and the flag also reaches the operator through the pending decision file's evidence_packet. Flagging the judgment call in case the reviewer wants it explicit.
deferred_items: Detector recall is bounded by review_finding_classifier's anchor extraction and by resolvability: a window where any spanning family's description is ambiguous produces no signal at all. This is the conservative direction the uncertainty AC requires, but noisy multi-concern windows will rarely fire. Giving classify_families a stable per-finding identity key (rather than matching on a description prefix) would raise recall and remove the whole unresolvable-family class; out of scope here.

Not a defect in this change, but observed every iteration: running the test suite (tests/test_cut_rc_isolation.py) mutates the tracked file src/theforge/sprint/runner.py in the working tree, and git stash in this worktree then leaves conflict markers in it. Restored from HEAD and verified clean before each commit (git diff HEAD -- src/theforge/sprint/runner.py is empty). Worth a separate bug.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 adds a top-level key to the canonical audit record but modifies tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v23.json. The repository is currently at CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION = 26 in src/theforge/coordinator/audit_substrate.py, and tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py requires any writer-shape change to bump the schema, add MIGRATION_HELPERS[26], and create audit_record_schema_v27.json. As written, CI will fail the schema guard.
  Suggestion: Replace the v23 fixture change with a v26-to-v27 audit-schema update: bump CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION, add _migrate_v26_to_v27 and MIGRATION_HELPERS[26], and generate tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v27.json.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 3 appends parsed_review before _run_escalate_gate(), but the gate's approve path already calls _append_cycle_history(state, approvable). An operator accept would therefore record the detected cycle twice and could evict an earlier entry from the three-entry cycle_history window.
  Suggestion: Make cycle-history insertion idempotent for this path, or teach the gate that the current history entry was already appended, while still ensuring the advisor packet includes the triggering cycle.
- [P2] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 4 adds early-detection evidence but does not explicitly update build_advisor_prompt()'s hardcoded statement that review cycles 'were exhausted,' which is false for this new pre-ceiling route.
  Suggestion: Make the advisor introduction describe a generic escalation or distinguish topology-triggered escalation from cycle exhaustion.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 names tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v23.json, but CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION (audit_substrate.py:89, re-exported as SCHEMA_VERSION in coordinator/audit.py:19) is 26. Adding a top-level audit key is a field-set change that tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py::test_audit_record_schema_unchanged fails on; editing the v23 fixture will not satisfy it, and the plan does not mention the SCHEMA_VERSION bump or the paired MIGRATION_HELPERS entry the guard requires.
  Suggestion: Follow the procedure the guard's own failure message spells out: bump CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION to 27, add MIGRATION_HELPERS[26] = _migrate_v26_to_v27, regenerate with REGENERATE_AUDIT_SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT=1 and commit the NEW tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v27.json — do not edit v23.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] The new audit key is not added to PRIOR_GENERATION_WORK_KEYS (src/theforge/sprint/audit.py:1733). A story that escalates on the topology signal and then hits an abnormal exit would lose the signal from the carried-forward record, which is exactly the case where the evidence matters most.
  Suggestion: Add the new key alongside finding_registry in PRIOR_GENERATION_WORK_KEYS.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3's continue path is described only as 'clear the active escalation enough to re-enter normal REVIEW/RETRY_DEV flow'. The existing analogous path (review_phase.py:2209-2212) returns RETRY_DEV leaving state.phase == ESCALATE, and the interactive surface is handled by a separate _handle_interactive_review_decision branch that the plan does not mirror.
  Suggestion: Mirror the max-cycle branch's continue semantics exactly (minus the review_cycle decrement, which is correctly omitted here), and decide explicitly whether the interactive path should also detect or fall through to the existing per-cycle behaviour.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Detection at trajectory_cycle 3 is inert when config.retry.max_review_cycles is 3 or lower, since the guard requires review_cycle < _adaptive_review_max and the ceiling branch already fires there. Also note trajectory_cycle and review_cycle diverge (trajectory_cycle is never decremented by extend/reject/gate-continue), so the two counters must not be compared directly.
  Suggestion: Key the ceiling guard on review_cycle and the family-span check on trajectory_cycle, and cover the small-ceiling case in tests so the detector degrades to existing behaviour rather than double-escalating.
- [P2] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] Step 2 of the plan references tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v23.json, but the actual codebase is currently at schema version v26 (making audit_record_schema_v26.json the active snapshot, and requiring v27 if a new field is added).

finding_registry.description: When three cycles contain a recurring P2-only family and the current cycle also has an unrelated blocking P1, the detector reports a topology walk for the P2 family and the review phase can escalate even though the blocking P1 is not the discovered sibling path.

When a three-cycle window contains one resolvable P1 walk and another P1 family whose recorded member maps to multiple concrete findings, the detector emits a topology-walk signal for the resolvable family and the review phase can escalate even though multiple blocking concerns are in flight.
When three blocking findings share the same anchor at three different locations but reuse identical finding text, the detector returns no topology signal and the review loop keeps spending cycles.
When a topology signal is computed on the ceiling cycle instead of triggering early routing, the advisor prompt still says the escalation fired before review cycles were exhausted.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
